title: Trump says pardon for Jensen Huang is ‘always an option’ but likely won’t be needed | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

President Donald Trump said Tuesday he would be open to pardoning newly reinstated Nvidia CEOJensen Huangfor any potential crimes — but he added that it likely won’t be needed.

“It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary,” Trump told theNew York Postin an interview when asked about pardoning Huang.

The president also urged Huang to “tell the truth” when facingbipartisan questioningfrom Congress next week. CNN previously reported that Huang is set to testify behind closed doors on Capitol Hill Tuesday, and he will appear in a public hearing with lawmakers next Thursday.

“I don’t think he needs to take the Fifth. I think it’s an interesting story for people,” Trump said.

“I think I want him to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I’ve always found him to be 100% aboveboard, and you know a very smart person,” the president said.

Trump’s comments come a day afterNvidia’s board brought Huang back as CEO. Hereturned to the chipmaker’s headquarters to loud cheers and applause from employees.

During Tuesday’s interview, the Post reported, Trump didn’t hide his satisfaction with how the market responded onceNvidia stock rose more than 30% Mondayafter the board’s decision, checking the latest numbers at the Resolute Desk and pointing out that the stock had recovered.

“That’s not bad, went down a couple of points,” Trump said, “it really picked up at the end.”

Correction:This story has been updated to correct Jensen Huang will appear in a public hearing on Capitol Hill next Thursday.
